sections.title: Overview
sections.body:
**Project 8:** BREAST CANCER DETECTION

**What you'll learn:**
- CROSS-VALIDATION deep dive — every method!
- KFold vs StratifiedKFold vs RepeatedStratifiedKFold
- cross_val_score vs cross_val_predict
- Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV)
- Why cross-validation MATTERS and when to use which

**Dataset:** Breast Cancer Wisconsin (sklearn built-in)
- 30 features (mean, error, worst of 10 cell measurements)
- Binary: Malignant (0) or Benign (1)
- 569 samples

**Type:** BINARY CLASSIFICATION + Cross-Validation Deep Dive

data = load_breast_cancer()

X = df.drop("target", axis=1)

sections.title: Step 4: Cross-Validation Deep Dive
sections.body:
```python
cv_explanation = """
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║               CROSS-VALIDATION - COMPLETE GUIDE                     ║
╠══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                      ║
║  WHY Cross-Validation?                                               ║
║  ─────────────────────                                               ║
║  Single train/test split is DANGEROUS:                               ║
║  - Results depend on WHICH data points are in train vs test          ║
║  - You might get lucky or unlucky with the split                     ║
║  - Cross-validation gives you a RELIABLE estimate                    ║
║                                                                      ║
║  METHODS:                                                            ║
║  ─────────                                                           ║
║  1. KFold: Split data into K parts, train on K-1, test on 1         ║
║     - Good for regression                                            ║
║     - Doesn't preserve class distribution!                           ║
║                                                                      ║
║  2. StratifiedKFold: Same as KFold but preserves class ratios        ║
║     - ALWAYS use for classification!                                 ║
║     - Each fold has same % of each class                             ║
║                                                                      ║
║  3. RepeatedStratifiedKFold: Repeats StratifiedKFold N times         ║
║     - Different random splits each time                              ║
║     - Most reliable but slower                                       ║
║                                                                      ║
║  4. LeaveOneOut (LOOCV): K = number of samples                       ║
║     - Train on all but 1, test on that 1                             ║
║     - VERY slow for large datasets                                   ║
║     - Low bias, high variance                                        ║
║                                                                      ║
║  COMMON CHOICES:                                                     ║
║  - Small dataset (<500): RepeatedStratifiedKFold(5, n_repeats=3)     ║
║  - Medium dataset (~1000): StratifiedKFold(5 or 10)                  ║
║  - Large dataset (>10000): StratifiedKFold(5)                        ║
║                                                                      ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
"""
print(cv_explanation)

# === Method 1: KFold ===
print("=" * 60)
print("METHOD 1: KFold (Basic)")
print("=" * 60)

kf = KFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)
model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=5000, random_state=42)

# Show fold contents
print("\nFold details:")
for fold_num, (train_idx, test_idx) in enumerate(kf.split(X_train_s), 1):
    train_target = y_train.iloc[train_idx]
    test_target = y_train.iloc[test_idx]
    train_pct = train_target.mean()
    test_pct = test_target.mean()
    print(
        f"  Fold {fold_num}: Train={len(train_idx)} (benign:{train_pct:.1%}) | "
        f"Test={len(test_idx)} (benign:{test_pct:.1%})"
    )

kf_scores = cross_val_score(model, X_train_s, y_train, cv=kf, scoring="accuracy")
print(f"\nKFold scores: {kf_scores}")
print(f"KFold mean: {kf_scores.mean():.4f} ± {kf_scores.std():.4f}")

# === Method 2: StratifiedKFold ===
print("\n" + "=" * 60)
print("METHOD 2: StratifiedKFold (PRESERVES CLASS RATIOS)")
print("=" * 60)

skf = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)

print("\nFold details:")
for fold_num, (train_idx, test_idx) in enumerate(skf.split(X_train_s, y_train), 1):
    train_target = y_train.iloc[train_idx]
    test_target = y_train.iloc[test_idx]
    train_pct = train_target.mean()
    test_pct = test_target.mean()
    print(
        f"  Fold {fold_num}: Train={len(train_idx)} (benign:{train_pct:.1%}) | "
        f"Test={len(test_idx)} (benign:{test_pct:.1%})"
    )

skf_scores = cross_val_score(model, X_train_s, y_train, cv=skf, scoring="accuracy")
print(f"\nStratifiedKFold scores: {skf_scores}")
print(f"StratifiedKFold mean: {skf_scores.mean():.4f} ± {skf_scores.std():.4f}")
print("\n→ NOTICE: Class ratios are CONSISTENT across folds! (unlike KFold)")

# === Method 3: RepeatedStratifiedKFold ===
print("\n" + "=" * 60)
print("METHOD 3: RepeatedStratifiedKFold (MOST RELIABLE)")
print("=" * 60)

rskf = RepeatedStratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, n_repeats=3, random_state=42)
rskf_scores = cross_val_score(model, X_train_s, y_train, cv=rskf, scoring="accuracy")
print(f"\nRepeatedStratifiedKFold: 5-fold × 3 repeats = {len(rskf_scores)} evaluations")
print(f"Scores: {rskf_scores}")
print(f"Mean: {rskf_scores.mean():.4f} ± {rskf_scores.std():.4f}")
print("\n→ 15 evaluations = more reliable estimate than just 5!")

# === Method 4: LeaveOneOut ===
print("\n" + "=" * 60)
print("METHOD 4: Leave-One-Out CV (LOOCV)")
print("=" * 60)

loo = LeaveOneOut()
print(f"Number of folds: {loo.get_n_splits(X_train_s)} (= n_samples!)")
print("Running LOOCV (this takes time for large datasets)...")

loo_scores = cross_val_score(model, X_train_s, y_train, cv=loo, scoring="accuracy")
print(f"LOOCV accuracy: {loo_scores.mean():.4f} ± {loo_scores.std():.4f}")
print("→ LOOCV has lowest bias but highest variance and is SLOWEST")
```

sections.title: Step 5: Visual Comparison Of Cv Methods
sections.body:
```python
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(18, 5))

# Compare CV score distributions
cv_data = {
    "KFold(5)": kf_scores,
    "StratifiedKFold(5)": skf_scores,
    "RepeatedSKF(5×3)": rskf_scores,
}

# Box plot
positions = range(len(cv_data))
bp = axes[0].boxplot(
    cv_data.values(),
    labels=cv_data.keys(),
    patch_artist=True,
    boxprops=dict(facecolor="lightblue"),
)
axes[0].set_ylabel("Accuracy")
axes[0].set_title("CV Method Comparison")
axes[0].tick_params(axis="x", rotation=15)

# cross_val_score with multiple scorers for same model
scorers = ["accuracy", "precision", "recall", "f1", "roc_auc"]
results = {}
for scorer in scorers:
    scores = cross_val_score(model, X_train_s, y_train, cv=skf, scoring=scorer)
    results[scorer] = scores.mean()

bars = axes[1].barh(list(results.keys()), list(results.values()), color="steelblue")
axes[1].set_xlim(0.9, 1.0)
for bar, val in zip(bars, results.values()):
    axes[1].text(
        val + 0.001, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height() / 2, f"{val:.4f}", va="center"
    )
axes[1].set_title("Multiple Metrics via cross_val_score")

# cross_val_predict confusion matrix
y_cv_pred = cross_val_predict(model, X_train_s, y_train, cv=skf)
cm = confusion_matrix(y_train, y_cv_pred)
sns.heatmap(
    cm,
    annot=True,
    fmt="d",
    cmap="Blues",
    ax=axes[2],
    xticklabels=["Malignant", "Benign"],
    yticklabels=["Malignant", "Benign"],
)
axes[2].set_title("cross_val_predict Confusion Matrix")
axes[2].set_xlabel("Predicted")
axes[2].set_ylabel("Actual")

plt.suptitle("Cross-Validation Deep Dive", fontsize=16, fontweight="bold")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("project_08_cv_comparison.png", dpi=150)
plt.show()
```

sections.title: Step 6: Compare Models Using Best Cv Method
sections.body:
```python
print("\n" + "=" * 60)
print("MODEL COMPARISON USING RepeatedStratifiedKFold")
print("=" * 60)

models = {
    "Logistic Regression": LogisticRegression(max_iter=5000, random_state=42),
    "KNN": KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=5),
    "SVM (RBF)": SVC(kernel="rbf", probability=True, random_state=42),
    "Random Forest": RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=200, random_state=42),
    "Gradient Boosting": GradientBoostingClassifier(n_estimators=200, random_state=42),
}

cv = RepeatedStratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, n_repeats=3, random_state=42)
all_scores = {}

print(f"\n{'Model':<25} {'CV Accuracy':>12} {'CV F1':>12} {'CV AUC':>12}")
print("-" * 65)

for name, model in models.items():
    acc = cross_val_score(model, X_train_s, y_train, cv=cv, scoring="accuracy")
    f1 = cross_val_score(model, X_train_s, y_train, cv=cv, scoring="f1")
    auc = cross_val_score(model, X_train_s, y_train, cv=cv, scoring="roc_auc")
    all_scores[name] = acc
    print(
        f"{name:<25} {acc.mean():>8.4f}±{acc.std():.3f} "
        f"{f1.mean():>8.4f}±{f1.std():.3f} "
        f"{auc.mean():>8.4f}±{auc.std():.3f}"
    )
```

sections.title: Step 7: Final Evaluation On Test Set
sections.body:
```python
best_model = SVC(kernel="rbf", probability=True, random_state=42)
best_model.fit(X_train_s, y_train)
y_pred = best_model.predict(X_test_s)
y_proba = best_model.predict_proba(X_test_s)[:, 1]

print(f"\n{'='*60}")
print("FINAL TEST SET EVALUATION")
print(f"{'='*60}")
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred, target_names=["Malignant", "Benign"]))

fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 5))

# Confusion Matrix
cm = confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred)
sns.heatmap(
    cm,
    annot=True,
    fmt="d",
    cmap="Blues",
    ax=axes[0],
    xticklabels=["Malignant", "Benign"],
    yticklabels=["Malignant", "Benign"],
)
axes[0].set_title("Confusion Matrix")

# ROC Curve
fpr, tpr, _ = roc_curve(y_test, y_proba)
auc = roc_auc_score(y_test, y_proba)
axes[1].plot(fpr, tpr, "b-", label=f"AUC = {auc:.4f}")
axes[1].plot([0, 1], [0, 1], "r--")
axes[1].set_xlabel("False Positive Rate")
axes[1].set_ylabel("True Positive Rate")
axes[1].set_title("ROC Curve")
axes[1].legend()

# CV scores boxplot
axes[2].boxplot(all_scores.values(), labels=[n[:12] for n in all_scores.keys()])
axes[2].set_ylabel("Accuracy")
axes[2].set_title("Model CV Scores")
axes[2].tick_params(axis="x", rotation=45)

plt.suptitle("Final Evaluation", fontsize=16)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig("project_08_final.png", dpi=150)
plt.show()

# Save
pipeline = Pipeline([("scaler", StandardScaler()), ("model", best_model)])
pipeline.fit(X_train, y_train)
joblib.dump(pipeline, "project_08_breast_cancer_pipeline.pkl")
print("✓ Pipeline saved!")

print(
    """
KEY TAKEAWAYS - CROSS-VALIDATION:
  1. ALWAYS use StratifiedKFold for classification (preserves class ratios)
  2. KFold is OK for regression (or StratifiedKFold with binned targets)
  3. RepeatedStratifiedKFold = most reliable (but slower)
  4. LeaveOneOut = lowest bias but highest variance, slowest
  5. cross_val_score → returns SCORES array
  6. cross_val_predict → returns PREDICTIONS (for confusion matrix, etc.)
  7. Small datasets → use more repeats (n_repeats=5 or 10)
  8. Large datasets → 5-fold is usually enough
  9. NEVER evaluate on training data! Always use CV or held-out test set
  10. For MEDICAL data: Recall (sensitivity) is more important than accuracy!
"""
)
```
